summary:
StarMed ("Because someone has to care for those who reach the stars and the moon") is an interactive health-monitoring prototype designed to support astronauts' physical and mental well-being on deep-space missions, prepared to immediately inform astronauts on what to do in case of an emergency.
Through a friendly, illustrated medical assistant and an interactive astronaut body interface, users can easily monitor six vital indicators (heart rate, blood pressure, glucose, temperature, sleep, and mood) with clear microgravity measurement instructions and color-coded traffic-light alerts (green, yellow, red). To address spaceflight hazards like microgravity, radiation, and isolation, StarMed adapts health recommendations to specific environments (spaceship, space station, rover, or lunar/Martian base), includes a zero-gravity SOS first-aid guide, and encourages daily check-ups through wellness badges and family connection features.
StarMed is important because it reduces human error and anxiety during medical emergencies, making space healthcare intuitive, preventive, and emotionally supportive for future explorers.
details:
How it works & Benefits: StarMed is an interactive visual prototype designed using custom illustrations. Crew members tap parts of an interactive astronaut body (heart, head, arm) to follow step-by-step microgravity measurement guides and see color-coded traffic-light alerts (green, yellow, red). It also adapts health advice to four space environments (spaceship, station, rover, lunar/Martian base), includes a zero-gravity SOS first-aid guide, and motivates daily check-ups with wellness badges.
Tools, Creativity & Considerations: Developed with Canva and original hand-drawn artwork inspired by empathetic medical companions and NASA Human Research Program data. We considered real spaceflight challenges like communication delays with Earth, microgravity fluid shifts, radiation, isolation, and non-medical crews needing calm, error-free interfaces during emergencies.
